extraction.name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
extraction.description: A comprehensive benchmark designed to assess AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing. It comprises 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories, including natural sounds, music, spoken dialogue, multi-turn dialogue, role-play imitation, and heterogeneous images.
extraction.creator: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li
extraction.publisher: CUHK MMLab, SenseTime Research, CPII under InnoHK
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected by extracting diverse visual and auditory inputs from 37 existing datasets. Text instructions were converted to audio using TTS models. A multi-stage curation process involving deduplication, validation, categorization, and sampling was applied to ensure quality.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Incomplete or unsuitable instances, including entries with corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, and demonstrably incorrect answers, were excluded. Approximately 10% of candidates were discarded during the validation stage.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 37 datasets including natural sounds, music, dialogue, and various images. Specific sources include LibriSpeech, Common Voice, Clotho, AudioCaps, AVQA, MusicCaps, MUSIC-AVQA, MMMU, RoleBench, and others listed in Table 8 of the paper.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Text instructions were preprocessed for TTS: special tokens were replaced with descriptive phrases, text was rewritten using Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct for TTS suitability, and multiple-choice options were rephrased. Speech was synthesized using F5TTS, ChatTTS, and Dia-1.6B, evaluated with UTMOS (regenerated if score < 3.8), and transcribed with Whisper to select the sample with the lowest word error rate.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A four-stage curation process: (1) Deduplication using lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance; (2) Validation to exclude incomplete/unsuitable items; (3) Categorization into 13 predefined task categories based on source metadata; (4) Balanced sampling to equalize category representation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Reference answers were derived from source datasets and validated by human curators using a web-based tool who assigned Good/Bad verdicts based on media integrity, task well-posedness, and answer validity. Model evaluation involves a Triadic System: content quality assessed by gpt-oss-20b, speech quality by UTMOS, and consistency by modified WER. For role-play, speaker similarity is calculated using Wespeaker.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Validation of the automated evaluation scheme showed high alignment with human judgments: an overall Pearson correlation of 0.92 and an agreement rate of 96.1% between gpt-oss-20b and human evaluations.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: F5TTS, ChatTTS, Dia-1.6B, UTMOS Strong, Whisper-Large-v3, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, gpt-oss-20b, emotion2vec, Wespeaker
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: A data governance process will be maintained for auditing and removal, and the creators reserve the right to update assets if consent or licensing concerns arise.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Voice data and role profiles (100 distinct roles with audio clips) are used. The benchmark emphasizes strict consent, provenance, and anti-impersonation safeguards to mitigate identity spoofing risks.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Potential misuse risks include identity spoofing, harassment, and fraud. Measures are taken to minimize harms related to impersonation, privacy violations, and unequal performance across demographics.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may carry biases from source data and design choices (academic/synthetic sources). The role-play subset uses a fixed set of 100 roles which may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas. The monolingual focus (English) limits diversity.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Monolingual focus (mostly English), limited range of evaluated models (mostly open-source), reliance on automated/GPT-based scoring which may introduce noise/bias, gaps in task coverage (no video-audio integration or continuous streaming), and static offline evaluation not capturing latency or barge-in handling.
